title: Add installable PWA support, offline app shell, and local notifications

requirements.summary: Make the app installable (PWA) via manifest, icons, and required HTML metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: The app includes a valid web app manifest (webmanifest) with name, short_name, start_url, display=standalone, theme_color, background_color, and icons.
frontend/index.html links the manifest and includes appropriate meta tags for PWA installation.
The app provides at least 192x192 and 512x512 app icons referenced by the manifest.
On supported browsers (e.g., Chrome Android), the app is eligible for Add to Home Screen and launches in standalone mode after installation.

file_operations.description: Add a valid web app manifest with name/short_name, start_url, display=standalone, theme_color, background_color, and icons referencing frontend/public/assets/generated/pwa-icon.dim_192x192.png and frontend/public/assets/generated/pwa-icon.dim_512x512.png.
Link the web app manifest and add PWA-related metadata (including theme color and install-related tags) required for installability.
Add the generated PWA app icon asset (192x192) at this exact path and ensure it matches the manifest reference.
Add the generated PWA app icon asset (512x512) at this exact path and ensure it matches the manifest reference.

requirements.summary: Register a service worker and provide minimal offline app-shell caching with an offline fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: A service worker is registered from editable application code (do not modify immutable paths).
When the app is installed, reopening it while offline shows either cached app shell or an explicit offline fallback page/message.
Service worker updates are handled safely (new SW activates without breaking navigation; users are not stuck on an old cached version indefinitely).

file_operations.description: Add a minimal service worker that caches the app shell (main HTML/CSS/JS and key static assets) and serves a basic offline fallback for navigations when offline.
Add a simple offline fallback page/message that the service worker can return for navigation requests when the cache cannot satisfy the request.
Implement service worker registration from editable application code, including safe update handling (detect new SW, prompt/auto-reload strategy, and avoid indefinite staleness).
Wire service worker registration into the app startup (without modifying frontend/src/main.tsx) by calling the registration utility from a top-level component effect.

requirements.summary: Add a dismissible in-app install prompt UX using beforeinstallprompt and standalone detection.
acceptanceCriteria: When the browser fires beforeinstallprompt, the UI shows an install call-to-action.
Clicking the install call-to-action triggers the native install prompt.
After installation (or when running in standalone), the install call-to-action is hidden or replaced with an 'Installed' indicator.
The install UI can be dismissed and does not reappear immediately in the same session after dismissal.

file_operations.description: Create a hook that listens for beforeinstallprompt, exposes an install trigger, detects standalone/installed state, and tracks per-session dismissal to avoid immediate reappearance.
Add a small, dismissible install banner/button component that uses the PWA install hook to show CTA, trigger prompt, and display an Installed indicator when appropriate.
Render the install banner in a visible, non-intrusive place within the existing layout (e.g., near header/main content) so it is available across pages without introducing a new route.
Add localized Farsi strings for the install CTA, Installed indicator, and dismiss action.

requirements.summary: Add Settings UI for Web Notifications permission, status display, and test notification.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings page includes a Notifications section with: permission status, a button to request permission, and a button to send a test notification.
If permission is denied, the UI clearly indicates that notifications are blocked and the test notification action is disabled or explains why it cannot run.
If permission is granted, clicking test sends a visible system notification with a sensible title and body.
No notification permission prompt is shown automatically on page load; it is only triggered by an explicit user action.

file_operations.description: Create a hook wrapping the Web Notifications API to read permission status, request permission only on explicit user action, and send a test notification when allowed.
Add a Settings section UI that shows notification permission status, a request-permission button, and a test-notification button with clear disabled/blocked states.
Wire the Notifications section into the existing Settings page (no new top-level pages/routes).
Add localized Farsi strings for notification permission states, request permission action, and test notification labels/messages.

requirements.summary: Show deduplicated in-app reminders (and optional system notifications) for meaningful events derived from existing loaded tasks/work items while app is open.
acceptanceCriteria: When the app is open and the user has granted notification permission, the app can emit a system notification for at least one meaningful event derived from existing state (e.g., detecting overdue items on load or after data refresh).
When permission is not granted, the same event is still surfaced as an in-app notification/toast (no silent failure).
Reminder behavior avoids spamming: the same reminder is not repeatedly shown on every render; it is deduplicated per session (or with a simple timestamp/seen tracking in localStorage).

file_operations.description: Implement reminder detection using existing React Query state (e.g., overdue tasks via dueDate and new/overdue work inbox items), deduplicate reminders per session or via localStorage, and emit either an in-app toast or system notification when permission is granted.
Create a non-visual component that subscribes to existing data hooks (tasks and work inbox items) and triggers reminders through the reminders hook.
Wire the RemindersListener into the app shell so reminders can run while the user navigates the app (without modifying restricted files and without creating orphan components).
